test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What are the four tax rates in India under GST?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5%, 12%, 18% and 28%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **GST tax slab of 5%**

 
 
• Goods – Spices, chapati, edible oil, bread, pizza bread, fish, Khakhra, tea and coffee, etc.

 Services – aircraft lease, crude and petroleum transport, takeaway food, economy flight tickets, etc.
 
 
 
• **GST tax slab of 6%**
 
 
• Goods – Frozen meat, meat sausages, juices, sauces, cakes, pickles, boiled sugar, products made of milk, etc.

 Services – Business class flight tickets, movie tickets, hotel stay (Price 
 
 
• **GST tax slab of 18%**
 
 
• Goods – Mineral water, raw pasta, biscuits, pastries, soup, cornflakes, curry powder and paste, etc.

 Services – Movie tickets (> INR 100), Hotel accommodation (>= INR 7,500), Daily room (from INR 2,500 and 5,000), etc.
 
 
 
• **GST tax slab of 28%**
 
 
• Goods – Aerated water (with or without added sugar), instant coffee, chocolates, protein, coffee and custard concentrates, etc.

 Services – Hotel stay wherein bill is > INR 7,500, gambling, go-karting, ballet, club services such as casinos, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GST has been structured in a way that essential services and food items are placed in the lower tax brackets.
 
• Luxury services and products have been placed in the higher tax bracket.
 
• The GST council has fitted over **1300 goods** and **500 services** under four tax slabs of **5%, 12%, 18% and 28%.**
 
• A total of **81%** of all the goods and services fall below or in the **18%** tax slab.
 
• **7%** of the items come under the exempted list,** 14%** of the items attract a 5% tax and** 17%** of the items attract a **12%** tax.
 
• **43%** of the items attract an **18%** tax slab, while only **19% **of the items fall under the highest slab of **28%** in the new regime.
